correctness.rationale: In K6−M3=K_{2,2,2} a singleton fails fort and the only inclusion-minimal local forts are three mate pairs and eight transversal triples; every size>=4 contains such a fort. For hub-free global F, each nonempty page must be a local fort, and the hub sees >=2; minimality forces precisely one local minimal fort (3r+8r). For hub-containing F each page must dominate, which requires >=2 vertices: all pairs dominate, any page with >2 selected permits reduction. A mate pair alone is a proper hub-free fort, while a nonmate pair alone is NOT fort, hence a globally minimal hub-containing fort consists of precisely one nonmate pair on every page; 12 choices/page and 12^r such forts. For r=1 coefficients at z³ combine as 8+12. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all subsets for r=1,2,3 recovered exact profiles and tested proper subforts. Infinite classification rests on the block argument. Growth exponent uses |V|=6r+1; sixth powers compare 12>9.
